Sprinkenhof in the Kontorhausviertel, Hamburg, Germany
The Kontorhaus district, with its brick expressionist office buildings, was created in the 1920s as a globally unique, purely commercial district based on the North American model under the direction of Hamburg’s chief architect Fritz Schumacher. Today, together with the Speicherstadt, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The development was a response to the cramped, overpopulated alleyways of the old town and the need for modern office space for the Hanseatic city’s burgeoning international trade. Among the most famous buildings are the iconic Chilehaus, reminiscent of a ship’s bow, the Sprinkenhof, the Meßberghof, and the Mohlenhof. Despite being designed by different architects (including Fritz Höger, who designed the Chilehaus, as well as Hans Gerson and Oskar Gerson), the district exudes a remarkable sense of unity.
